case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses Bluetooth SIG qualification strategy for a module-based BLE product during and after the transition to the new Qualification Workspace and QPRD-based process. The customer initially planned to combine a qualified Controller Subsystem and a qualified Component-based host stack, then sought guidance on the most efficient registration path. The discussion evolved as the new qualification system introduced Consistency Check behavior that generated additional test requirements when overlapping protocol layers were referenced. The final registration was completed using a simplified qualification reference strategy and successfully advanced to the review stage despite a TCW-related Consistency Check warning.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The primary technical issue was how to qualify a product built from a qualified Controller Subsystem and a qualified host-stack Component while avoiding unnecessary testing. Under the new Qualification Workspace introduced in July 2024, overlapping Core Layer coverage between referenced designs can trigger additional lower-layer test requirements through Consistency Check processing. The consultant determined that referencing only the BLE Solution qualification produced equivalent ICS coverage without the overlapping-layer problem and therefore avoided new test requirements. The thread also clarifies that a TCW-related message shown on the review page can be acceptable and does not necessarily block submission when the waiver has been properly incorporated into the qualification workflow.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant compared the qualification coverage and ICS content of the available referenced designs and found that the desired functionality could be represented without combining overlapping qualification layers. Because the new qualification process evaluates referenced Core Layers during Consistency Check, avoiding redundant layer references eliminates unnecessary test-plan generation. The final decision favored the qualification path that achieved the same functional coverage while minimizing qualification complexity and test exposure.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If overlapping qualified designs are combined unnecessarily under the new qualification process, Consistency Check may generate additional lower-layer test requirements. Existing module-vendor test evidence may not satisfy the newly generated requirements, creating avoidable qualification work, added cost, and schedule delay. Misinterpreting the TCW-related review-page warning as a submission blocker could also delay an otherwise valid qualification filing.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: An early conclusion stated that redundant protocol layers contained within a referenced Component could simply be excluded during design registration and would not create a qualification issue. After the new Qualification Workspace behavior was evaluated, it became clear that overlapping Core Layer references could trigger Consistency Check-driven test requirements. The recommendation was therefore revised to avoid overlapping references altogether and use the simpler qualification path.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Under the post-July-2024 Bluetooth SIG qualification process, always analyze Core Layer overlap and Consistency Check behavior before combining multiple referenced QDIDs. The technically simplest qualification architecture is often the best qualification architecture, especially when it provides equivalent ICS coverage while avoiding unnecessary test-plan generation and qualification risk.
